decisions.reason: F1 wrongly attributed Fermi coordinates, density and the Laplacian to the metric definition. The global result was already imported in F3; corrected the defining citations and attributed Fermi coordinates to the consulted Lemma 3.5. Checked the complete Proposition 3.1 construction, density normalization, the orientation-cover mixed terms, and the elementary one-dimensional case; the Statement is unchanged.

The usual sufficiently-small semiclassical threshold h_0 was left unquantified. The commutator proof is valid after choosing h_0 below both the convexification bound and C_0 h_0 ||q||_infinity <= 1/2. Made this existential threshold explicit, uniform in the two signs, and recorded both bounds in step 3.1; no all-h estimate is asserted. Hahn–Banach and Riesz then give the stated distributional solver.

The objection overlooks the cited supplier proof: lem-ip-conductivity-map-wellposedness step 1.1 explicitly proves bounded endpoint evaluation, collar lifts, and the endpoint-zero H1 kernel by |u(t)|^2 <= t integral_0^t |u prime|^2, cutoff approximation and mollification. This applies to the arbitrary extension difference W, exactly as Verification 1.1 says. The resulting H0^1 test makes both weak pairings independent of lifts; higher-dimensional trace localization and outward Green fluxes are sound. The item is unchanged.

The connectedness hypothesis of F3 was omitted. Compact smooth closure has finitely many components, each with nonempty boundary; applying solvability componentwise and taking the maximum Poincare constant proves exactly the original correction estimate. Repaired F3 and step 5.1. Also repaired the reader-confirmed phase expansion in 5.2 by adding exp(-2 lambda x_n) O(lambda^2 x_n^2), clarified the final uncanceled transport term, and extended the norm lower bound over bounded parameter intervals. The weighted limit constant remains k!/2^k and the Statement is unchanged.

F3 accidentally attached the zero trace condition to the forcing F. Its actual supplier requires zero solution boundary value and allows arbitrary H^k forcing. Corrected that restatement. The proof already uses the stronger correct interface: energy and componentwise Poincare establish the Laplacian kernel condition, then G acts on arbitrary H^{s-2}; the cubic map is a smooth real Banach polynomial and D_w F(0,0)=Id. Thus the existing IFT and normal-trace argument proves the unchanged Statement.

F5 omitted the Euclidean Green supplier's n>=2 hypothesis; its use did not justify n=1. Restricted that restatement to its actual range and supplied the one-dimensional second Green identity directly by the fundamental theorem of calculus in arclength charts, including counting boundary density and the left/right outward signs. Elliptic regularity makes the differentiated fields smooth, and the cubic derivative is 6v1v2v3. The original all-dimensional Statement and the positive sign of the boundary integral are preserved.

The tau-dependence allegation is false: the actual local supplier Proof 2.1 uses contraposition of density, chooses S=integral Q product(w_j) nonzero, and scales one factor by T/S; these smooth Q-dependent witnesses really are constant in tau. They are not the Gaussian families used to prove density in LL–LS. Independently confirmed the digest's nonfatal defect in F5: [F1] incorrectly named the small-data lemma as the simple-surface definition. Corrected that reference and clarified the two constructions. Third-linearization gives the zero product integral, the local witnesses give every longitudinal Fourier integral, and Fourier uniqueness plus continuity yields the unchanged claim.

F2 omitted the boundary-determination theorem's n>=2 and choice hypotheses. Its use was nonessential to the explicit counterexample: a nonzero smooth bump supported in radius 1/2 changes the interior and vanishes near the boundary, also on the interval. Corrected F2 to its actual scope and made it contextual rather than a proof input. In one dimension the DN map is governed by integral(1/gamma), so no DN-to-all-jets implication is asserted there. Positivity, flatness, and inequality at the origin prove the unchanged Example.
